technical_and_design_decisions: Use Java 17+ as required by Spring Framework 6.0
Use AWS SDK v2 for the Kinesis sink module implementation
Port XD modules following the existing s-c-s module conventions (configuration metadata, binder abstraction, tests)
Build the Job DSL on top of Spring Cloud Task / Spring Batch primitives to leverage existing scheduling and orchestration support
Implement the Flink processor as a thin s-c-s module wrapping Flink DataStream API operators, with a clear separation between the s-c-s binding layer and the Flink job graph
Use Maven as the build tool (consistent with the Spring ecosystem), JUnit 5 for unit tests, and TestContainers / embedded servers for integration tests
Treat counter-style modules (field-value-counter, aggregate-counter, gauge, rich-gauge) as MetricSink implementations backed by an in-memory store with optional external persistence
assumptions: The original Spring XD source code is available and accessible as a reference for porting
The developer is familiar with the Spring Cloud Stream programming model (channels, binders, suppliers/consumers)
AWS credentials and a reachable Kinesis stream are available for end-to-end testing of the Kinesis sink
A working Flink cluster (local or remote) can be provisioned for testing the Flink processor module
No major refactoring of the s-c-s core framework is required; the work is additive (new modules) plus a porting effort
One workday equals 8 hours of focused development effort
Estimates include unit tests and module-level integration tests but exclude the time required to set up dedicated CI infrastructure (assumed to already exist)
Requirements (U1–U8) are independently implementable; no cross-module blocking dependencies that would require sequential, calendar-stretched work

activities.activity_description: Study the existing s-c-s repository layout, module conventions, and build configuration; set up new Maven modules for Kinesis, Flink, and the Job DSL; design the shared abstraction layer for the ported counter modules.

Implement a new s-c-s sink binder for Amazon Kinesis using AWS SDK v2, including configuration metadata, partition key handling, batching, retries, and integration tests against an embedded/local Kinesis-compatible mock.
Port the XD Log sink module to s-c-s, adapting the logger configuration (level, name, custom converter) and ensuring compatibility with the s-c-s Message and channel model.

Design and implement a fluent job DSL that allows users to declaratively define tasks/steps, dependencies, and triggers; integrate it with the existing s-c-s deployment / launcher model and provide an embedded mode for local runs.
Port the XD field-value-counter sink to s-c-s as a MetricSink that counts occurrences of a configured field value, including expiration / sliding window options and tests.
Port the XD aggregate-counter sink to s-c-s, supporting per-key aggregation with configurable aggregation functions (count, sum, min, max, avg) and a reset/trigger mechanism.
Port the XD gauge sink to s-c-s as a simple MetricSink that exposes the latest value of a metric via the metrics endpoint.
Port the XD rich-gauge sink to s-c-s, extending the simple gauge with average, max, min, and count statistics maintained over a configurable time window.

Implement an s-c-s processor that submits a configured Flink streaming job, wiring s-c-s input/output channels to Flink DataStream sources/sinks, and providing a starter for the streaming-ML abstractions.

End-to-end test scenarios that exercise the new modules together in sample streaming pipelines (e.g., source → field-value-counter → Kinesis; source → Flink processor → log sink; Job DSL orchestrating a multi-step pipeline).
Write reference documentation for each new module (Kinesis, Job DSL, Flink, ported counters) covering configuration options, sample usage, and migration notes for XD users.
